standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicial objects, N and s
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a simplicial object V of an abelian category, the associated chain complex s(V) and the normalised complex N(V), and the canonical morphism between them.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the objects of the statement (source lines 4146-4149).

standard_prerequisites.name: Eilenberg-MacLane objects and skeletal filtrations
standard_prerequisites.statement: The objects K(A,k), their description as i_{k!} sk_k of the skeleton, and the injectivity of the natural map K(V_m,m) to V for V concentrated in degrees at least m (the author's lemma-homology-eilenberg-maclane, lemma-N-K, lemma-eilenberg-maclane-object, definition-eilenberg-maclane and lemma-n-skeleton-abelian, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: They provide the base case and the splitting used in the induction step (source lines 4155-4179).

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of N and s
standard_prerequisites.statement: The functors N and s send admissible short exact sequences of simplicial objects to short exact sequences of complexes (the author's lemmas lemma-s-exact and lemma-N-exact, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: They produce the morphism of short exact sequences from which the long exact sequence comparison is read off (source lines 4183-4200).

standard_prerequisites.name: The decomposition s = N direct sum D
standard_prerequisites.statement: The canonical morphism N(V) to s(V) is split with a functorial complement D(V) (the author's lemma-decompose-associated-complexes, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the statement's reformulation, and it is what makes the acyclicity formulation available (source lines 4150-4151).

core_obligations: Settle the Eilenberg-MacLane case: prove the statement for the objects K(A,k) for every A and k (source lines 4155-4158).
Set up the double induction: state the hypothesis IH_{n,m} and observe that IH_{n,n} is trivial because both complexes vanish in degree n (source lines 4158-4168).

Make the induction step: for V with V_j = 0 for j < m, use the skeleton identification to embed K(V_m,m) into V, obtain the short exact sequence with quotient W concentrated in degrees at least m+1, and record the induced morphism of short exact sequences of complexes (source lines 4169-4199).
Conclude by exactness: deduce the statement for V from the statement on the two ends via the long exact sequence in homology (source lines 4200-4201).

proof_roadmap.step: Prove the case of the Eilenberg-MacLane objects K(A,k).
State the induction hypothesis IH_{n,m} and check the trivial initial case IH_{n,n}.
Split V through K(V_m,m) and obtain the short exact sequence with quotient W concentrated in higher degrees.
Use exactness of N and s to get the morphism of short exact sequences and conclude for V from the ends.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-quasi-isomorphism at source lines 4144-4152: for a simplicial object V of an abelian category the canonical morphism N(V) to s(V) is a quasi-isomorphism, equivalently the complement D(V) of the previous lemma is acyclic. The proof at source lines 4154-4202 is a double induction: it first notes the result for the objects K(A,k), then states the hypothesis IH_{n,m} for simplicial objects concentrated in degrees at least m, observes that IH_{n,n} is trivial, and in the induction step splits V through the skeleton inclusion K(V_m,m) = i_{m!} sk_m V into a short exact sequence whose quotient W is concentrated in degrees at least m+1, uses the induced morphism of short exact sequences of the complexes N and s (which needs both exactness lemmas) and the long exact sequence to deduce the statement for V from its ends. The bookkeeping of the two induction indices and the identification of the quotient are the substance; the statement itself is one line.
